claims.text: A hierarchical multi-fidelity ML interatomic-potential framework can accurately calculate solid–liquid free-energy differences near fusion.
On-the-fly perturbative corrections can recover anharmonic and electron–vibration coupling contributions to phase free energies.
The proposed framework will reduce cost by roughly one order of magnitude relative to explicit ab initio molecular dynamics.
The proposed framework will reduce cost by about 50% relative to TOR-TILD.
Elemental, binary, and multicomponent high-entropy systems near melting exhibit significant vibrational, anharmonic, and electron–vibration features.
An interatomic potential can represent relevant structural and high-temperature behavior in a five-component high-entropy alloy.
Training the ML-IAP on ab initio data for both solid and liquid phases will make it suitable for fusion free-energy calculations.
The method is intended to operate within 200 K above or below the melting point.
The method will first be benchmarked on elemental and binary systems such as aluminum and iron before extension to a five-component high-entropy alloy.
The ML-IAP can mimic the complex energy landscapes of both solid and liquid phases.
On-the-fly reweighting can adjust free-energy estimates to restore missing anharmonic and electron–vibration coupling contributions.
An ML potential approximates interatomic forces at lower cost than full ab initio molecular dynamics.
Integrated perturbative corrections continuously refine free energies by capturing vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling.
The method will reproduce fully converged ab initio phase free energies within ±5 meV/atom.
The method will predict melting temperatures within ±200 K of the ab initio reference.

Classical molecular-dynamics potentials for quinary Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni can quantitatively reproduce selected structural properties, relative stability, pair probabilities, and high-temperature short-range ordering from first-principles calculations or experiment.
CoCrFeMnNi exhibits temperature-dependent polymorphic stability between fcc and hcp structures.
Prior elemental and binary evidence supports the feasibility of ML-IAPs with on-the-fly corrections.
Multicomponent interactions in high-entropy alloys may reduce the accuracy of free-energy reweighting.
The benchmark will compare solid and liquid free energies, melting temperature, and latent heat against converged ab initio molecular dynamics and TOR-TILD.
